*.text: Oklahoma context: the whole state is in the Southwest Power Pool. OG&E and PSO (an AEP company) file generation preapproval and certificate cases at the Oklahoma Corporation Commission; cases filed since March 2022 need a sign-in to search, so the daily Public Utility Division docket PDFs and the harvest file batches/us-ok/harvest/psc_dockets.md are the way in. Air permits in process sit in the Oklahoma DEQ Permits for Public Review table and their documents (applications, draft permits, notices, from 2016 on) are in scopes/us-ok/work/permits/<plant_id>.md. Permits older than 2016 are not online; say 'open records request needed' rather than searching again. Cooperatives (Western Farmers, Associated Electric, Grand River Dam Authority, OMPA, Peoples Electric) do not file at the commission; their record is the SPP queue, the DEQ permit and their own reports. Amalia Llano edited many Oklahoma rows on 2026-10-29, 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-04, and added Comanche CC2 and CC3, Northeastern Unit 5 and Unit 6, Port of Inola, Citadel Facility Data Center and Project Thunderbird; treat the export values as her baseline and stage a change against one only when a verified document disagrees.

OG&E resource plans: the 2024 IRP, the 2025 IRP update (its 2025 request for proposals selected Horseshoe Lake units 13 and 14) and the 2026 IRP. The 2026 IRP PDF is on OGE Energy's investor site (ogeenergy.gcs-web.com, needs the browser-fingerprint route in fetch.py) and the commission's copy of the 2025 IRP is at https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/occ/documents/pud/reports/2025-oge-irp.pdf. Extracted copies, if the harvest step made them, are under scopes/us-ok/work/irp/. For every OG&E plant (Horseshoe Lake, Mustang, Seminole, McClain, Redbud, Frontier, Muskogee, Tinker, River Valley, Charles D. Lamb through OMPA) check the plan for a start date, a retirement year or a capacity that disagrees with the export, cite the PDF page, and give the reviewer an IRP Notes line. The US IRPs tab matched no plant automatically because it names the utility OG&E and the export says Oklahoma Gas and Electric.

PSO resource plans: the 2024 IRP and the 2026 IRP Refresh on PSO's website (plain fetch works). They cover the Comanche combined cycle additions (ERAS-2025-024 and ERAS-2025-026), the Northeastern gas turbine (ERAS-2025-023), the Green Country acquisition and the retirement dates at Northeastern 3, Riverside, Southwestern, Tulsa, Weleetka and Comanche. Cite the page.

L100000402231.text: Comanche (OK) power station: Amalia added CC2 and CC3 on 2026-11-04 (686.4 MW each, PSO, 2029, pre-construction). Verify them; do not add them again. Sources: SPP ERAS-2025-024 and ERAS-2025-026 (775.2 MW each, Lawton East Side and Oklaunion to Lawton 138 kV, interconnection agreement executed, 2029-04-01), EIA-860M September 2026 plant 8059 (generators 2G1 408.8 MW and 2S1 277.6 MW, 3G1 and 3S1 the same, planned for 2029), ODEQ permit 2022-0055-C M-1 in process, PSO's 2026 IRP Refresh, and the OCC preapproval cause from the daily dockets. Report owner PSO at 100 percent, the turbine model, a Latest Activity date, and a question naming which EIA generator ids belong to each block.

L100000104126.text: Northeastern Station: Amalia added Unit 5 and Unit 6 on 2026-11-04 (225 MW each, 2028, pre-construction, GE turbines with the model unknown) and set Unit 3 timepoint 2 to operating with a 2041 planned retirement. Check the two new units against SPP ERAS-2025-023 (one 513 MW gas turbine, Oologah 345 kV, 2029-11-01) and the ODEQ permits 2019-0607-C M-2 to M-4: unit count, capacity and start year. Find the turbine model in the permit. EIP lists the Unit 3 gas timepoint as proposed and the Sierra Club list as planned; answer both with a public source. The one Sierra Club sheet row to fill is Northeastern 3.

L100000402162.text: Horseshoe Lake: units 11 and 12 are operating 2026 in GEM and 'construction complete, testing' for October 2026 in the September EIA-860M file; a status change needs two independent publishers. Units 13 and 14 (224 MW, 2029 in GEM, February 2029 in EIA) sit beside ERAS-2025-010 (496 MW gas turbine, 2028-04-01) and GEN-2024-GR1 (492 MW, executed); unit 15 (755 MW, 2031) beside ERAS-2025-004 (756.2 MW combined cycle, 2029-04-01): the dates disagree, ask in a question. Steam unit 7 (220 MW) and unit 6 (163 MW) retired in 2024 per EIA; say where they are in GEM. Units 8, 9 and 10 planned retirements against the 2026 IRP. DEQ permit 2024-0324-ARR5 M-2 in process. Unit 6 and ST7 are retired 2024 in GEM since Amalia's 2026-11-03 edits, matching EIA; confirm their source.

L100000401595.text: Redbud: SPP ERAS-2025-003 (186 MW combined cycle addition, Luther 345 kV, 2025-10-24) with the OG&E 2026 IRP is a new unit GEM lacks; stage it at the plant with the owner shares from EIA-860 (OG&E, OMPA, Grand River Dam Authority).

L100000104122.text: Grand River Energy Center: unit 4 is 594 MW in EIA and in SPP GEN-2024-GR5 (gas and storage hybrid, executed, commercial) against 426 MW in GEM; EIP and the Sierra Club list still say under construction. A capacity question naming both sources; status stays operating unless a document says otherwise. Unit 3's replacement link points at a unit that does not exist (validation fix). GEN-2025-SR19 (100 MW, Maid 161 kV, Chouteau) is a lead.

L100000402164.text: Mustang (OK) power station: 462 MW in GEM for units 6 to 12 against a 66 MW GT1 in EIA; the GEM row may be the whole plant of seven aeroderivative turbines. A capacity question with the unit convention from docs/reference/unit_conventions.md. SPP GEN-2025-SR23 (100 MW special study) and GEN-2016-047 (24 MW) are leads. The DEQ document store has no Mustang documents; do not search it again.

L100001063385.text: Tinker Air Force Base power station: EIA plant 63628 'Tinker' (Oklahoma County; generators 1 and 2 of 48.1 MW from 2026, 5A and 5B of 41 MW from 1971, out of service) is this site; write a question stating the match with the code and generator ids, for Baird to type into Other IDs. DEQ permits 2025-0595-C M-1 and TV in process (OG&E Tinker Turbines); SPP GEN-2023-GR2 (94.242 MW, executed). City is blank.

L100001089274.text: Bristow Energy Center: owner is blank and Associated Electric is the operator; stage the project company or the cooperative at 100 percent from a document. Location is approximate (location ladder). SPP GEN-2024-340 (1,440 MW, Creek County, AEP) is not this plant; find its own queue row or say none was found. Check the DEQ table for a permit application.

L100000104124.text: Muskogee Generating Station: three validation fixes, Owner 1 has no source, Location has no source, and the carbon capture field on units 4 and 5 timepoint 2 has no source. Units 4 and 5 timepoint 2 carry start year 2019, the conversion year, while EIA gives 1977 and 1978 for the original units; GEM's convention is the conversion year, so say so in a question rather than edit. SPP GEN-2025-SR9 (400 MW, OG&E, pending) and GEN-2024-293 (248 MW, Muskoge7, 2032) may be this plant or the Core Scientific data center plant.

L100001081005.text: Muskogee Data Center: Amalia set unit 1 to construction on 2026-11-04 (283.1 MW, Core Scientific, start 2026, Backup Power yes, ODEQ stored permit 9138 as the source). Check it against SPP GEN-2025-SR9 (400 MW) and GEN-2024-293 (248 MW) at Muskogee substations, the ODEQ permit and Core Scientific's filings; a Latest Activity date. County is filled now.

L100000402369.text: Anadarko: units 1 to 3 retired December 2024 per EIA, GEM agrees; EIP's 'under construction' row is Roulet 12 and 13 (50.2 MW each, construction), which match SPP GEN-2023-GR1 (97.488 MW, 69 kV, executed). Check the DEQ Western Farmers Anadarko row for the construction permit and a start date.

L100000104123.text: Hugo: Amalia added Site A (73.5 MW) and Site B (342 MW), pre-construction 2029, Western Farmers. SPP GEN-2026-SR34 (75 MW, Hugo 138 kV, Fort Towson) and GEN-2024-323 (372 MW, ITC Hugo 7 345 kV, 2029) are the queue rows; if the capacities disagree with hers, ask. City reads 'Fort Townsend'; the town is Fort Towson. EIA 6772 lists the coal unit only.

L100001023579.text: Ripley Energy Center: 445 MW in GEM against 419 MW in EIA (RP1, under construction, April 2027). A capacity question; check the DEQ permit and the owner.

L100001080983.text: Cross Timbers (Konawa, 255 MW, two units pre-construction): Amalia's Notes name construction permit 2025-0397-C; read it for turbines and the site. Latest Activity; duplicate check against the Seminole-area queue row GEN-2024-321 (507 MW, Seminole 345 kV, 2029).

L100001063386.text: Chickasha industrial park (500 MW): Amalia set it to cancelled on 2026-11-04 on a quote that the project was cancelled for site limitations in early 2026. EIP still lists it as proposed. Find the public source of the quote and a second publisher if one exists; a status change is green only on two. Location is approximate; the completed Assigned Comments thread on its technology is the baseline.

L100001082617.text: ONE Nuclear power station unit 1 (1,000 MW gas, announced): city and county blank; location ladder; Latest Activity; confirm the fuel is gas, not nuclear, from the source.

L100000401991.text: Green Country (795 MW, Jenks): PSO's acquisition. Stage an ownership change only on the closing document; before closing, a Status Detail entry on top. DEQ draft permit OK0043869 dated 2026-10-16 is in the document store.

L100000402165.text: Seminole (OK): city reads 'Konowa'; the town is Konawa. Planned retirements, moved by Amalia to 2031, 2033 and 2035, against the OG&E 2026 IRP. SPP GEN-2024-321 (507 MW, Seminole 345 kV, 2029) and a GEN-2025-SR special study at Seminole are leads.

L100000409256.text: Stillwater Energy Center: city now filled; SPP ASGI-2014-014 Ferguson (56.4 MW, Payne County) is probably this plant. Say so or say why not.

L100000401932.text: Spring Creek (Evergy Kansas Central): the Evergy IRP updates; SPP GEN-2024-255 (300 MW thermal and storage hybrid at Spring Creek 345 kV) is a lead, not this plant.

L100000402236.text: Weleetka: units 4 and 5 planned retirement 2030 against the PSO 2026 IRP Refresh.

L100001089319.text: Port of Inola Power Station (new plant, added by Amalia 2026-11-04): units 1A and 1B, 641 MW each, PSO, 2030, pre-construction, Rogers County. Verify; do not add again. Read the ODEQ PSD000139 permit application (object id 1153508 in the Permits for Public Review table) for the turbine model, the configuration behind two 641 MW units and the site; find the OCC cause and PSO's 2026 IRP Refresh line; a Latest Activity date. Amalia's Notes carry a permit table link; Notes stay as they are.

L100001089312.text: Citadel Facility Data Center at Sperry (new plant, added by Amalia 2026-11-04): units 1 and 2, 99 and 198 MW of diesel backup engines, Backup Power yes, pre-construction, location approximate. Her note says 118 engines in four groups: 36 Cummins DQLF at 2.75 MW and 72 Caterpillar 3516E or MTU 20V4000 at about 2.75 to 2.8 MW, plus the rest. Check the engine counts, per-engine ratings and the unit split against the ODEQ permit, apply the per-engine capacity rule, find the owner entity and the exact site, and add a Latest Activity date.

L100001089336.text: Project Thunderbird Data Center at Enid (new plant, added by Amalia 2026-11-04): 3,300 MW behind-the-meter gas plant for a four-campus data center, owner Plainsmen Holdings LLC, pre-construction, one unit row. Read the ODEQ permit, the Enid and Garfield County records and any SPP row for the turbines, the unit count, a start year and the site; confirm pre-construction rests on a permit application; a Latest Activity date. The duplicate check runs against the other Enid-area leads.
